newsitem.title: USA: Lawmakers introduce bill to repeal estate tax.
newsitem.headline: Lawmakers introduce bill to repeal estate tax.

text.p: Republican lawmakers Monday introduced legislation to repeal a tax on estates they termed the "death" tax, saying it hurts family businesses that are passed on to the next generation.
The repeal measure was introduced in the Senate in January and in the House of Representatives Monday.
Rep. Chris Cox, the bill's sponsor in the House, said the estate tax brings in less than 1 percent of federal revenue.

The congressional Joint Committee on Taxation estimates about $20 billion a year in revenues are collected from the estate tax and expects that amount to increase to $26 billion in 2002, a committee spokesman said.

The tax kicks in when the estate is valued at more than $600,000. The graduated rate scale reaches the highest tax rate of 55 percent on estates valued at $10 million to $21 million, the committee spokesman said.
Cox and other lawmakers said the estate tax can force family business owners and farmers to liquidate their businesses to pay the tax.
"When you have to sell the farm to save the farm, that's wrong," said Sen. Conrad Burns, a Republican from Montana.
